info.title: Conversión de index.html a gestor de proyectos

metadata.displayText:
Actúa como un Desarrollador Full-Stack Senior experto en UI/UX, arquitecturas Serverless y Google Apps Script. Estoy transformando un archivo `index.html` (adjunto) en una herramienta de gestión de proyectos para dos usuarios (José y Luis). 

El stack es: Vercel (Frontend y Serverless Functions) + Google Sheets (Base de Datos vía Google Apps Script). Las credenciales se manejarán como variables de entorno en Vercel.

REGLA DE ORO: BAJO NINGUNA CIRCUNSTANCIA alteres el estilo visual, los efectos 3D (neumorfismo), los colores (--neon, --bt-dia, --bt-cero), las fuentes (Orbitron) ni los iconos pixel-art existentes en el `index.html`. Debes mantener la estética exacta actual.

REQUERIMIENTOS DE LÓGICA Y UI (index.html):
1. Vista Semanal: Modifica el grid para mostrar solo los 7 días de la semana actual (Dom a Sáb). Los botones "‹" y "›" navegarán entre semanas. El título mostrará el rango (ej. "Sem 44: 27 Oct - 02 Nov").
2. Reubicación: Mueve el botón de tema (Sol/Luna) a la barra superior del header.
3. Barras de Progreso: 
   - En la barra de herramientas (donde estaban los iconos), pon una barra de progreso GENERAL (suma de José + Luis).
   - En el panel inferior, pon una barra de progreso PERSONAL. Añade un toggle o selector para cambiar de usuario (José/Luis).
4. Etiquetas: Las tareas tendrán una barra de color: Cian (--neon) para José y Magenta (--neon2) para Luis.
5. Modal "Minuta": Un botón abrirá un textarea para pegar texto. Al procesar, enviará el texto a la API.
6. Reemplaza `localStorage` por llamadas `fetch()` a nuestra API.

REQUERIMIENTOS DEL DASHBOARD (dashboard.html):
1. Crea un archivo separado `dashboard.html` que use el mismo CSS (puedes importar el mismo bloque de estilos o un archivo CSS compartido).
2. Debe mostrar métricas visuales (puedes usar CSS puro o Chart.js si lo consideras necesario, pero manteniendo el estilo neumórfico):
   - Total de tareas completadas vs. pendientes.
   - Rendimiento por usuario (José vs. Luis).
   - Velocidad de finalización (tiempo promedio por tarea, requiere un campo de fecha de creación y fecha de finalización).
3. Un botón/enlace para volver al calendario.

REQUERIMIENTOS DE BACKEND Y GOOGLE SHEETS:
1. Dame el código exacto de Google Apps Script que debo pegar en la hoja de cálculo (Extensiones > Apps Script). Este script debe tener un `doGet` (para leer las tareas) y un `doPost` (para guardar tareas y actualizar estados) y devolver JSON.
2. Dame el código para la Serverless Function de Vercel (ej. `/api/sync.js`) que actúe como puente seguro entre el HTML y Google Apps Script usando `fetch`.
3. Explica qué columnas exactas debe tener el Google Sheet (ID, Fecha, Titulo, Responsable, Estado, FechaCreacion, FechaFinalizacion).

INSTRUCCIONES DE ENTREGA:
1. El código HTML/JS del index semanal.
2. El código HTML/JS del dashboard.
3. El código de Google Apps Script (copiable).
4. El código de la Serverless Function para Vercel.
5. Instrucciones de configuración de Vercel y Google Sheets.

Empieza directamente con el código. Sé preciso y no rompas los estilos existentes. trabaja local y deja listos los archivos para subir a github, debes entregarme todo por separado css html js etc confirma que entiendes lo que tienes que hacer y no comiences hasta que te de la orden comenzar

```js
/**
 * DÍA CERO — API Google Apps Script (Google Sheets como base de datos)
 * ...
 */
const SHEET_NAME = 'Tareas';
const API_KEY = 'DIA_CERO_CAMBIA_ESTA_CLAVE';
const HEADERS = ['ID','Fecha','Titulo','Responsable','Estado','FechaCreacion','FechaFinalizacion','Hora'];

function getSheet_(){
  const ss = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet();
  let sh = ss.getSheetByName(SHEET_NAME);
  if(!sh){ sh = ss.insertSheet(SHEET_NAME); }
  if(sh.getLastRow() === 0){ sh.appendRow(HEADERS); sh.setFrozenRows(1); }
  return sh;
}

function json_(obj){ return ContentService.createTextOutput(JSON.stringify(obj)).setMimeType(ContentService.MimeType.JSON); }
function ok_(extra){ return json_(Object.assign({ok:true}, extra||{})); }
function err_(msg){ return json_({ok:false, error:msg}); }
function authorized_(e){ return !!e && e.parameter && e.parameter.key === API_KEY; }

function rowToTask_(r){
  return { id:String(r[0]||''), fecha:String(r[1]||''), titulo:String(r[2]||''), responsable:String(r[3]||''),
    estado:String(r[4]||'pendiente'), fechaCreacion:String(r[5]||''), fechaFinalizacion:String(r[6]||''), hora:String(r[7]||'') };
}

function readAll_(){
  const sh = getSheet_();
  const last = sh.getLastRow();
  if(last < 2) return [];
  const values = sh.getRange(2,1,last-1,8).getValues();
  return values.filter(r=>r[0]).map(rowToTask_);
}

function findRow_(sh, id){
  const last = sh.getLastRow();
  if(last < 2) return -1;
  const ids = sh.getRange(2,1,last-1,1).getValues();
  for(let i=0;i<ids.length;i++){ if(String(ids[i][0])===String(id)) return i+2; }
  return -1;
}

function newId_(){ return 'T-' + Utilities.getUuid(); }

function doGet(e){
  if(!authorized_(e)) return err_('No autorizado');
  const action = (e.parameter.action || 'getTasks');
  if(action === 'getTasks'){ return ok_({ tasks: readAll_() }); }
  return err_('Acción no válida: ' + action);
}

function doPost(e){
  if(!authorized_(e)) return err_('No autorizado');
  let body; try{ body = JSON.parse(e.postData.contents); }catch(err){ return err_('JSON inválido'); }
  const lock = LockService.getScriptLock();
  try{ lock.waitLock(20000); }catch(err){ return err_('Hoja ocupada, intenta de nuevo'); }
  try{
    const sh = getSheet_();
    const action = body.action;
    if(action === 'create'){
      const t = sanitize_(body.task, true);
      sh.appendRow([t.id,t.fecha,t.titulo,t.responsable,t.estado,t.fechaCreacion,t.fechaFinalizacion,t.hora]);
      return ok_({ task: t });
    }
    if(action === 'bulk'){
      const list = Array.isArray(body.tasks) ? body.tasks : [];
      if(!list.length) return err_('Lista vacía');
      const rows = list.map(raw=>{ const t=sanitize_(raw,true); return [t.id,t.fecha,t.titulo,t.responsable,t.estado,t.fechaCreacion,t.fechaFinalizacion,t.hora]; });
      sh.getRange(sh.getLastRow()+1, 1, rows.length, 8).setValues(rows);
      return ok_({ tasks: rows.map(r=>rowToTask_(r)) });
    }
    if(action === 'update'){
      const row = findRow_(sh, body.id); if(row<0) return err_('Tarea no encontrada');
      const current = rowToTask_(sh.getRange(row,1,1,8).getValues()[0]);
      const c = body.changes || {};
      const t = { ...current };  // ES5? Apps Script V8 supports spread. V8 runtime default yes.
      if(typeof c.titulo === 'string') t.titulo = c.titulo;
      if(typeof c.fecha === 'string') t.fecha = c.fecha;
      if(typeof c.responsable === 'string') t.responsable = c.responsable;
      if(typeof c.hora === 'string') t.hora = c.hora;
      if(typeof c.estado === 'string' && (c.estado==='pendiente'||c.estado==='completada')){
        t.estado = c.estado;
        t.fechaFinalizacion = (c.estado==='completada') ? (c.fechaFinalizacion || new Date().toISOString()) : '';
      }
      sh.getRange(row,1,1,8).setValues([[t.id,t.fecha,t.titulo,t.responsable,t.estado,t.fechaCreacion,t.fechaFinalizacion,t.hora]]);
      return ok_({ task: t });
    }
    if(action === 'delete'){
      const row = findRow_(sh, body.id); if(row<0) return err_('Tarea no encontrada');
      sh.deleteRow(row);
      return ok_({ deleted: body.id });
    }
    return err_('Acción no válida: '+action);
  } finally { lock.releaseLock(); }
}

function sanitize_(raw, withId){
  raw = raw || {};
  return {
    id: withId ? (raw.id || newId_()) : raw.id,
    fecha: String(raw.fecha || ''),
    titulo: String(raw.titulo || '').slice(0,120),
    responsable: (raw.responsable==='Luis') ? 'Luis' : 'José',
    estado: (raw.estado==='completada') ? 'completada' : 'pendiente',
    fechaCreacion: raw.fechaCreacion || new Date().toISOString(),
    fechaFinalizacion: raw.fechaFinalizacion || '',
    hora: String(raw.hora || '')
  };
}
```

# DÍA CERO — Gestión de proyectos (José & Luis)

Stack: **Vercel** (frontend + serverless) + **Google Sheets** (base de datos vía Google Apps Script).

## Estructura de archivos (lista para GitHub)

```
/
├── index.html            ← Calendario SEMANAL (Dom–Sáb)
├── dashboard.html        ← Dashboard de métricas
├── logo.jpeg
├── 2.png                 ← favicon / logo
├── titulo.png
├── old2.png
├── Captura de pantalla … ← capturas (opcionales en el repo)
├── css/
│   └── styles.css        ← CSS compartido (estilo original intacto + nuevos componentes)
├── js/
│   ├── api.js            ← cliente fetch() a /api/sync
│   ├── app.js            ← lógica del calendario semanal
│   └── dashboard.js      ← lógica del dashboard
├── api/
│   └── sync.js           ← Serverless Function de Vercel (puente a Apps Script)
├── apps-script/
│   └── Code.gs           ← código para Google Apps Script
└── README.md
```

---

## 1. Google Sheets + Google Apps Script

1. Crea una hoja de cálculo nueva en Google Drive (ej. `DIA_CERO_DB`).
2. **Extensiones > Apps Script** y pega todo el contenido de `apps-script/Code.gs`.
3. Cambia la constante secreta:
   ```js
   var API_KEY = 'DIA_CERO_CAMBIA_ESTA_CLAVE'; // ⚠️ pon tu propia clave
   ```
4. **Implementar > Nueva implementación > Aplicación web**:
   - Ejecutar como: **Yo**
   - Quién tiene acceso: **Cualquier persona**
5. Autoriza los permisos la primera vez y copia la **URL pública** (termina en `/exec`).
   → Esto será tu `GAS_URL`.
6. La hoja crea sola la pestaña **`Tareas`** con las columnas exactas:

| Columna | Campo | Descripción |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | `ID` | Identificador único (`T-<uuid>`). Nunca se edita a mano. |
| **B** | `Fecha` | Fecha de la tarea en formato `YYYY-MM-DD` (la usa el calendario). |
| **C** | `Titulo` | Texto de la tarea (máx. 120 caracteres). |
| **D** | `Responsable` | `José` o `Luis` (define el color de la barra: cian / magenta). |
| **E** | `Estado` | `pendiente` o `completada`. |
| **F** | `FechaCreacion` | ISO 8601 (`2026-11-01T14:30:00.000Z`). Se pone al crear. |
| **G** | `FechaFinalizacion` | ISO 8601. **La pone sola el script** al marcar `completada` y borra al reabrir. Es lo que alimenta la métrica de velocidad del dashboard. |
| **H** | `Hora` | *(opcional)* `HH:MM` para las alarmas de 5 minutos. |

> Si cambias `Code.gs`, vuelve a **Implementar > Administrar implementaciones > Editar > Implementar** para publicar la nueva versión (la URL no cambia).

---

## 2. Vercel

1. Sube el repo a GitHub y créalo en [vercel.com/new](https://vercel.com/new) (framework: **Other**).
2. En **Settings > Environment Variables** agrega:

   | Variable | Valor |
   |---|---|
   | `GAS_URL` | URL de Apps Script (la que termina en `/exec`) |
   | `API_SECRET` | **Exactamente la misma** clave que `API_KEY` en `Code.gs` |

3. Deploy. Vercel detecta automáticamente:
   - `/api/sync.js` → Serverless Function
   - `index.html`, `dashboard.html`, `css/`, `js/` → estáticos.

### Cómo fluyen los datos (seguridad)

```
index.html / dashboard.html
      │  fetch('/api/sync')      ← sin secretos
      ▼
api/sync.js (Vercel)             ← inyecta API_SECRET (variable de entorno)
      │  fetch(GAS_URL?key=…)
      ▼
Code.gs (Google Apps Script)      ← valida key, lee/escribe la hoja "Tareas"
      ▼
Google Sheets
```

El secreto **nunca** llega al navegador.

---

## 3. Desarrollo local

```bash
npm i -g vercel
vercel dev
```

Crea un archivo `.env.local` (no se sube a GitHub):

```
GAS_URL=https://script.google.com/macros/s/XXXX/exec
API_SECRET=tu-clave-secreta
```

---

## 4. Subir a GitHub

```bash
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Día Cero: calendario semanal + dashboard + API"
git branch -M main
git remote add origin https://github.com/TU_USUARIO/TU_REPO.git
git push -u origin main
```

---

## 5. Funcionalidades

### index.html (calendario semanal)
- Grid de **7 días** (Dom → Sáb) de la semana visible; `‹` `›` cambian de semana; `Hoy` vuelve a la semana actual.
- Título marquesina con rango: **"Sem 44: 27 Oct - 02 Nov"**.
- Botón de tema (Sol/Luna) reubicado en la **barra superior del header**.
- **Barra GENERAL** en la toolbar (suma José + Luis del día seleccionado).
- **Barra PERSONAL** en el panel inferior con toggle **JOSÉ / LUIS**.
- Barra de color por responsable: **cian `--neon` (José)**, **magenta `--neon2` (Luis)**; los puntos del día también.
- Modal **Minuta**: pega texto (una tarea por línea), eliges responsable y se crea todo por la API (`Ctrl+Enter` procesa).
- Todo el CRUD pasa por `fetch()` → `/api/sync` → Google Sheets.
- `localStorage` solo guarda preferencias de UI (tema, alarmas, usuario activo) — **ningún dato del proyecto**.

### dashboard.html
- Total completadas vs pendientes + avance global.
- Rendimiento José vs Luis (barras cian/magenta).
- Velocidad de finalización promedio (y por usuario) calculada con `FechaCreacion → FechaFinalizacion`.
- Botón `‹` / "Calendario" para volver y `↻` para actualizar.

### API (apps-script/Code.gs)
- `doGet` → `action=getTasks` (leer tareas).
- `doPost` → `action=create | update | delete | bulk` (escribir, con `LockService`).
- Respuesta JSON siempre con `{ ok: true/false, … }`.

---

## 6. Notas
- El sonido de "tarea completada" y las alarmas siguen intactos.
- Los estilos, colores (`--neon`, `--bt-dia`, `--bt-cero`), fuente Orbitron e iconos pixel-art **no se modificaron**: todo lo nuevo reutiliza el mismo lenguaje neumórfico.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Transform an `index.html` calendar into a full project-management tool (weekly view, dashboard, Google Sheets backend) for two users (José/Luis), then rebrand it from "Día Cero" to "One on One Business" with HD pixel icons, and get the whole stack (Vercel + Google Apps Script) connected and functional — now adding Gemini API to process the "Minuta" feature.

## Requirements
- **GOLD RULE**: Never alter existing visual style, 3D effects (neumorphism), colors (`--neon`, `--neon2`, `--bt-dia`, `--bt-cero`), Orbitron fonts, or existing pixel-art icons.
- Weekly view: 7 days (Dom–Sáb), ‹/› week navigation, title like "Sem 44: 27 Oct - 02 Nov".
- Theme button (Sol/Luna) in header top bar.
- General progress bar (José+Luis) in toolbar; personal progress bar in bottom panel with José/Luis toggle.
- Task color bars: cyan `--neon` = José, magenta `--neon2` = Luis.
- Modal "Minuta": textarea → send text to API; replace all `localStorage` with `fetch()` (only UI prefs may stay in localStorage).
- `dashboard.html` sharing same CSS: completed vs pending, José vs Luis, avg completion speed (needs FechaCreacion/FechaFinalizacion), link back to calendar.
- Deliverables as separate files (HTML/CSS/JS), ready for GitHub.
- **Rebrand**: eliminate everything saying "Día Cero" and old logo; new name "One on One Business", keep "Micro-tareas y Foco" subtitle; new logos in folder (one for black bg, one for white bg); redraw button icons as high-definition pixel art.
- **Gemini API** (current request): copy a Gemini API key so it processes the Minuta text.

## Decisions
- Architecture: `index.html/dashboard.html → fetch('/api/sync') → Vercel api/sync.js → Google Apps Script Code.gs → Google Sheet "Tareas"`.
- Sheet columns: A ID, B Fecha, C Titulo, D Responsable, E Estado, F FechaCreacion, G FechaFinalizacion, H Hora (optional) — auto-created by script.
- CSS extracted verbatim to shared `css/styles.css` + clearly marked "NUEVOS COMPONENTES" additions.
- API key generated and embedded: `5c8b8b0bb8826283abb1ed3122ca4a3c` (repo keeps placeholder `ONE_ON_ONE_CAMBIA_ESTA_CLAVE` for security).
- Logos: originals kept untouched; derived `logo-dark.png`, `logo-light.png` (alpha-trimmed), `favicon.png` created; theme-based swap via CSS.
- Icons redrawn as 15×15 matrices at 2px step (from 7×7 at 3px), same box-shadow technique.
- GAS bug fixed: `doPost` must validate key inside JSON body (`body.key`) AND query param — original only checked `e.parameter`, which would have broken all writes.
- Hardened `api/sync.js` with `looksLikeJson()` validation returning clear 502 errors.

## Work State
### Completed
- Full app built and locally tested (mock server): weekly grid, navigation, theme toggle, progress bars, minuta modal, task CRUD, dashboard metrics — 0 console errors.
- Rebrand complete: all "Día Cero" references removed (verified via grep), new logos, HD icons (25/25 automated GAS tests passed).
- Google Apps Script deployed: `https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbwWuyUsiM6j592TxaMhGdIGC91x_52PnUG3y4FtLJeva71w4INO-Wb6XLP8cH8n93UlDA/exec`
- Fixed 403 "Acceso denegado" (user changed deploy access to "Cualquier persona"); re-tested: **8/8 end-to-end tests passed** (create, read, complete w/ auto FechaFinalizacion, delete, sheet clean, reject without key).
- Files pushed to GitHub and deployed on Vercel; both env vars `GAS_URL` and `API_SECRET` added in Vercel (Production), confirmed by screenshot.
- **Pending from that point**: user needs to Redeploy in Vercel (Deployments → ⋯ → Redeploy) so env vars take effect — "listo" was said but redeploy status unverified.

### Active
- New request: integrate **Gemini API** so it processes the Minuta (paste text → AI splits/creates tasks). User said: "ahora solo queda copiar una api de gemini para que haga el pocesos de la minuta".

### Blocked
- Gemini API key not yet provided by user; need to decide where key lives (Vercel env var, serverless endpoint) and how minuta flow changes (currently `minutaProcessBtn` just splits lines client-side and POSTs `action: 'bulk'`).

## Next Move
1. Explain to user how to get a Gemini API key (Google AI Studio) and add it as Vercel env var (e.g., `GEMINI_API_KEY`) — key must never reach the browser.
2. Create a Vercel serverless endpoint (e.g., extend `/api/sync.js` or add `/api/minuta.js`) that calls Gemini to parse pasted minuta text into structured tasks (titulo, responsable, fecha, hora), returning them for `bulk` create.
3. Update `js/app.js` `minutaProcessBtn` handler to call that endpoint instead of simple line-splitting; keep exact neumorphic modal style.
4. Have user Redeploy Vercel with new env vars, then run end-to-end tests against live site (user's site URL never provided).

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: main weekly calendar (rebranded, dual-logo header/footer)
- `dashboard.html`: metrics dashboard
- `css/styles.css`: shared CSS (original verbatim + new components + logo swap + `.pxicon` margin -15px)
- `js/app.js`: calendar logic, HD ICONS (15×15), minuta modal handler at `minutaProcessBtn`, API calls
- `js/api.js`: `window.API` client for `/api/sync`
- `js/dashboard.js`: metrics + theme restore from localStorage
- `api/sync.js`: Vercel serverless bridge (env: `GAS_URL`, `API_SECRET`; has `looksLikeJson()`) — will be extended for Gemini
- `apps-script/Code.gs`: doGet/doPost, API_KEY = `5c8b8b0bb8826283abb1ed3122ca4a3c` (deployed version)
- `README.md`: setup instructions (structure, env vars, sheet columns)
- `/tmp/opencode/mock-server.js`, `/tmp/opencode/test-gas.js`: local test harnesses (may need recreation)
- `logo-dark.png`, `logo-light.png`, `favicon.png`, `logo con para fondo negro.png`, `logo con para fondo blanco.png`: brand assets

## Important Context
- GAS URL: `https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbwWuyUsiM6j592TxaMhGdIGC91x_52PnUG3y4FtLJeva71w4INO-Wb6XLP8cH8n93UlDA/exec`

- User is non-technical; give click-by-click instructions, verify each step with tests from assistant side

- Repo pushed to GitHub; local changes to `api/sync.js` (hardening) — confirm whether already pushed/redeployed

# Models

The models endpoint provides a way for you to programmatically list the available models, and retrieve extended metadata such as supported functionality and context window sizing. Read more in [the Models guide](/docs/models).

## Methods  {% id="methods" %}

{% table %}
  * Method
  * HTTP request

  ---

  * [Getting a model](/api-reference/models/get-model)
  *     {% mark class="http-get" %}{% icon name="south_west" /%}`GET`{% /mark %} `/v1beta/models/{model}`

    Gets information about a specific [`Model`](/api-reference/models#Resource:Model) such as its version number, token limits, [parameters](/docs/prompting-strategies#model-parameters) and other metadata.


  ---

  * [Listing models](/api-reference/models/list-models)
  *     {% mark class="http-get" %}{% icon name="south_west" /%}`GET`{% /mark %} `/v1beta/models`

    Lists the [`Model`s](/docs/models) available through the Gemini API.

{% /table %}

## Resources  {% id="resources" %}

### Model  {% id="Resource:Model" %}

Information about a Generative Language Model.

**Properties:**

**name**: {% mark %}required{% /mark %} `string`

The resource name of the [`Model`](/api-reference/models#Resource:Model). Refer to [Model variants](/docs/models#model-versions) for all allowed values. Format: `models/{model}` with a `{model}` naming convention of:

- "{base_model_id}-{version}"

Examples:

- `models/gemini-1.5-flash-001`

{% hr /%}

**baseModelId**: {% mark %}required{% /mark %} `string`

The name of the base model, pass this to the generation request. Examples:

- `gemini-1.5-flash`

{% hr /%}

**version**: {% mark %}required{% /mark %} `string`

The version number of the model. This represents the major version (`1.0` or `1.5`)

{% hr /%}

**displayName**: `string`

The human-readable name of the model. E.g. "Gemini 1.5 Flash". The name can be up to 128 characters long and can consist of any UTF-8 characters.

{% hr /%}

**description**: `string`

A short description of the model.

{% hr /%}

**inputTokenLimit**: `integer`

Maximum number of input tokens allowed for this model.

{% hr /%}

**outputTokenLimit**: `integer`

Maximum number of output tokens available for this model.

{% hr /%}

**supportedGenerationMethods**: `array (string)`

The model's supported generation methods. The corresponding API method names are defined as Pascal case strings, such as `generateMessage` and `generateContent`.

{% hr /%}

**temperature**: `number`

Controls the randomness of the output. Values can range over `[0.0,max_temperature]`, inclusive. A higher value will produce responses that are more varied, while a value closer to `0.0` will typically result in less surprising responses from the model. This value specifies default to be used by the backend while making the call to the model.

{% hr /%}

**maxTemperature**: `number`

The maximum temperature this model can use.

{% hr /%}

**topP**: `number`

For [Nucleus sampling](/docs/prompting-strategies#model-parameters). Nucleus sampling considers the smallest set of tokens whose probability sum is at least `top_p`. This value specifies default to be used by the backend while making the call to the model.

{% hr /%}

**topK**: `integer`

For Top-k sampling. Top-k sampling considers the set of `top_k` most probable tokens. This value specifies default to be used by the backend while making the call to the model. If empty, indicates the model doesn't use top-k sampling, and `top_k` isn't allowed as a generation parameter.

{% hr /%}

**thinking**: `boolean`

Whether the model supports thinking.

This includes the extension of the file (e.g. `apps/admin/api/my-function.js` is 29 characters) - No spaces are allowed. Replace them with a `-` or `_` (e.g. `api/my function.js` isn't allowed) ## Bundle size limits Vercel places restrictions on the maximum size of the deployment bundle for functions to ensure that they execute in a timely manner. For Vercel Functions, the maximum uncompressed size is **250 MB** including layers which are automatically used depending on [runtimes](/docs/functions/runtimes). These limits are [enforced by AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html). For [Python functions](/docs/functions/runtimes/python), the maximum uncompressed size is **500 MB**. You can use [`includeFiles` and `excludeFiles`](/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json#functions) to specify items which may affect the function size. These configurations are not supported in Next.js, instead use [`outputFileTracingIncludes`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/output). ## Large functions Beta Large functions let you deploy uncompressed bundles up to **5 GB**. Use them for workloads that ship large dependencies, model files, or binaries. Large functions are supported on Node.js, Bun, and Python runtimes. Large functions require [fluid compute](/docs/fluid-compute) with [Active CPU](/docs/functions/usage-and-pricing#active-cpu) enabled. Fluid compute is enabled by default for new projects. ### Enable large functions New projects are eligible for large functions by default. For existing projects, opt in by setting the `VERCEL_SUPPORT_LARGE_FUNCTIONS` [environment variable](/docs/environment-variables). The environment variable always takes precedence over the project default. Set it to `1` to enable support for large functions, or `0` to disable, for both new and existing projects. You can set `VERCEL_SUPPORT_LARGE_FUNCTIONS` as a project [environment variable](/docs/environment-variables) in your project settings or with the [Vercel CLI](/docs/cli/env). In eligible projects, Vercel only uses the large functions beta for Functions that exceed the standard bundle size limit. Functions that fit within the standard limit continue to use the standard path. ### Supported runtimes Large functions are supported on the following runtimes: - [`nodejs`](/docs/functions/runtimes/node-js) - [`bun`](/docs/functions/runtimes/bun) - [`python`](/docs/functions/runtimes/python) > **💡 Note:** Large functions are not yet supported for projects using > [Secure Compute](/docs/networking/secure-compute) or > [Static IPs](/docs/networking/static-ips). ## Max duration This refers to the longest time a function invocation can run before Vercel terminates it. For request handlers, this includes time spent processing the request and sending the response, including streamed responses. While Vercel Functions have a default duration, this duration can be extended using the [maxDuration config](/docs/functions/configuring-functions/duration). If a Vercel Function doesn't complete within the duration, a 504 error code ([`FUNCTION_INVOCATION_TIMEOUT`](/docs/errors/function_invocation_timeout)) is returned. With [fluid compute](/docs/fluid-compute) enabled, Vercel Functions have the following defaults and maximum limits: ### Node.js, Bun, and Python runtimes | | Default | Maximum | Extended maximum | | ---------- | ---------------- | ------- | ---------------- | | Hobby | 300s (5 minutes) | 300s (5 minutes) | - | | Pro | 300s (5 minutes) | 800s | 1800s (30 minutes) Beta | | Enterprise | 300s (5 minutes) | 800s | 1800s (30 minutes) Beta | > **💡 Note:** The 800 second maximum is generally available for Pro and Enterprise teams. > The 1800 second extended maximum is in beta. Values above 800 seconds require > function-level configuration and are only supported for specific Node.js, > Bun, and Python runtime versions. [Secure Compute](/docs/networking/secure-compute) > and [Static IPs](/docs/networking/static-ips) do not support durations above > 800 seconds during the beta. See [configuring maximum > duration](/docs/functions/configuring-functions/duration#extended-max-duration-beta) > for the supported runtimes and examples. > **💡 Note:** For workloads that require unlimited execution time, use [Vercel > Workflows](/docs/workflows), which allow your code to pause, resume, and > maintain state for minutes to months without duration limits. ### Edge runtime Vercel Functions using the [Edge runtime](/docs/functions/runtimes/edge) must begin sending a response within 25 seconds to maintain streaming capabilities beyond this period, and can continue [streaming](/docs/functions/streaming-functions) data for up to 300 seconds. ## Memory size limits Vercel Functions have the following defaults and maximum limits: | | Default | Maximum | | ---------------- | ------------- | ------------- | | Hobby | 2 GB / 1 vCPU | 2 GB / 1 vCPU | | Pro / Enterprise | 2 GB / 1 vCPU | 4 GB / 2 vCPU | Users on Pro and Enterprise plans can [configure the default memory size](/docs/functions/configuring-functions/memory#setting-your-default-function-memory-/-cpu-size) for all functions in the dashboard. The maximum size for a Function includes your JavaScript code, imported libraries and files (such as fonts), and all files bundled in the function. If you reach the limit, make sure the code you are importing in your function is used and is not too heavy. You can use a package size checker tool like [bundle](https://bundle.js.org/) to check the size of a package and search for a smaller alternative. ## Request body size In Vercel, the request body size is the maximum amount of data that can be included in the body of a request to a function. The maximum payload size for the request body or the response body of a Vercel Function is **4.5 MB**. If a Vercel Function receives a payload in excess of the limit it will return an error [413: `FUNCTION_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`](/docs/errors/function_payload_too_large). See [How do I bypass the 4.5MB body size limit of Vercel Functions](/kb/guide/how-to-bypass-vercel-body-size-limit-serverless-functions) for more information. ## File descriptors File descriptors are unique identifiers that the operating system uses to track and manage open resources like files, network connections, and I/O streams. Think of them as handles or references that your application uses to interact with these resources. Each time your code opens a file, establishes a network connection, or creates a socket, the system assigns a file descriptor to track that resource. Vercel Functions have a limit of **1,024 file descriptors** shared across all concurrent executions. This limit includes file descriptors used by the runtime itself, so the actual number available to your application code will be strictly less than 1,024. File descriptors are used for: - Open files - Network connections (TCP sockets, HTTP requests) - Database connections - File system operations If your function exceeds this limit, you might encounter errors related to "too many open files" or similar resource exhaustion issues. To manage file descriptors effectively, consider the following: - Close files, database connections, and HTTP connections when they're no longer needed - Use connection pooling for database connections - Implement proper resource cleanup in your function code ## API support | | Support | | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | | Geolocation data | [Yes](/docs/headers/request-headers#x-vercel-ip-country) | | Access request headers | Yes | | Cache responses | [Yes](/docs/caching/cdn-cache#using-vercel-functions) | ## Cost and usage The Hobby plan offers functions for free, within [limits](/docs/limits). The Pro plan extends these limits, and charges usage based on active CPU time and provisioned memory time for Vercel Functions. Active CPU time is based on the amount of CPU time your code actively consumes, measured in milliseconds. Waiting for I/O (e.g. calling AI models, database queries) does not count towards active CPU time. Provisioned memory time is based on the memory allocated to your function instances multiplied by the time they are running. It is important to make sure you've set a reasonable [maximum duration](/docs/functions/configuring-functions/duration) for your function. See "Managing usage and pricing for [Vercel Functions](/docs/functions/usage-and-pricing)" for more information. ## Environment variables If you have [fluid compute](/docs/fluid-compute) enabled, the following environment variables are not accessible and you cannot log them: - `AWS_EXECUTION_ENV` - `AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER` - `AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_MEMORY_SIZE` - `AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME` - `AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_VERSION` - `AWS_LAMBDA_INITIALIZATION_TYPE` - `AWS_LAMBDA_LOG_GROUP_NAME` - `AWS_LAMBDA_LOG_STREAM_NAME` - `AWS_LAMBDA_RUNTIME_API` - `AWS_XRAY_CONTEXT_MISSING` - `AWS_XRAY_DAEMON_ADDRESS` - `LAMBDA_RUNTIME_DIR` - `LAMBDA_TASK_ROOT` - `_AWS_XRAY_DAEMON_ADDRESS` - `_AWS_XRAY_DAEMON_PORT` - `_HANDLER` - `_LAMBDA_TELEMETRY_LOG_FD` --- [View full sitemap](/docs/sitemap) If you encounter incorrect information, can’t find what you need, need a capability Vercel doesn’t currently offer, or have any other feedback to report, please do it by following the instructions at https://vercel.com/feedback.md.

responseSchema format (Gemini API v1beta):
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "tasks": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "titulo": {"type": "string"},
```

## Model version name patterns  {% id="model-versions" %}

Gemini models are available in either *stable*, *preview*, *latest*, or
*experimental* versions.

{% callout type="note" %}
  Note: The following list refers to the model string naming convention as of
  September, 2025. Models released prior to that may have different naming
  conventions. Refer to the exact model string if you are using an older model.

{% /callout %}

### Stable  {% class="hide-from-toc" id="stable" %}

Points to a specific stable model. Stable models usually don't change. Most
production apps should use a specific stable model.

For example: `gemini-3.6-flash`.

### Preview  {% class="hide-from-toc" id="preview" %}

Points to a preview model which may be used for production. Preview models will
typically have billing enabled, might come with more restrictive rate limits and
will be deprecated with at least 2 weeks notice.

For example: `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-09-2025`.

### Latest  {% class="hide-from-toc" id="latest" %}

Points to the latest release for a specific model variation. This can be a
stable, preview or experimental release. This alias will get hot-swapped with
every new release of a specific model variation. A **2-week notice** will be
provided through email before the version behind latest is changed.

For example: `gemini-flash-latest`.

### Experimental  {% class="hide-from-toc" id="experimental" %}

Points to an experimental model which will typically not be suitable for
production use and come with more restrictive rate limits. We release
experimental models to gather feedback and get our latest updates into the hands
of developers quickly.

Experimental models are not stable and availability of model endpoints is
subject to change.

## Model deprecations  {% id="model-deprecations" %}

For information about model deprecations, visit the [Gemini
deprecations](/docs/deprecations) page.

## Model version name patterns  {% id="model-versions" %}

Gemini models are available in either *stable*, *preview*, *latest*, or
*experimental* versions.

{% callout type="note" %}
  Note: The following list refers to the model string naming convention as of
  September, 2025. Models released prior to that may have different naming
  conventions. Refer to the exact model string if you are using an older model.

{% /callout %}

### Stable  {% class="hide-from-toc" id="stable" %}

Points to a specific stable model. Stable models usually don't change. Most
production apps should use a specific stable model.

For example: `gemini-3.6-flash`.

### Preview  {% class="hide-from-toc" id="preview" %}

Points to a preview model which may be used for production. Preview models will
typically have billing enabled, might come with more restrictive rate limits and
will be deprecated with at least 2 weeks notice.

For example: `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-09-2025`.

### Latest  {% class="hide-from-toc" id="latest" %}

Points to the latest release for a specific model variation. This can be a
stable, preview or experimental release. This alias will get hot-swapped with
every new release of a specific model variation. A **2-week notice** will be
provided through email before the version behind latest is changed.

For example: `gemini-flash-latest`.

### Experimental  {% class="hide-from-toc" id="experimental" %}

Points to an experimental model which will typically not be suitable for
production use and come with more restrictive rate limits. We release
experimental models to gather feedback and get our latest updates into the hands
of developers quickly.

Experimental models are not stable and availability of model endpoints is
subject to change.

## Requirements
- **GOLD RULE**: Never alter existing visual style, 3D effects (neumorphism), colors (`--neon`, `--neon2`, `--bt-dia`, `--bt-cero`), Orbitron fonts, or existing pixel-art icons.

MISIÓN: Refactorizar y escalar la aplicación web "One on One Business" para elevarla a nivel corporativo (Enterprise Grade), implementando tres módulos críticos de forma limpia, modular y segura:

1. RE-BRANDING UI/UX CORPORATIVO:
- Eliminar cualquier estética lúdica o informal. Migrar el sistema de diseño hacia una paleta sobria (fondos neutrales oscuros `bg-slate-950` o claros estructurados con bordes sutiles `border-gray-200`, acentos en azul corporativo `indigo-650`/`blue-700`).
- Densificar la información típica de dashboards ejecutivos utilizando tipografías limpias, tablas estructuradas (`divide-y divide-gray-200`), y tarjetas modulares con metadatos claros.
- Estandarizar componentes de estado (badges con bordes atenuados para completado, pendiente, en progreso).

2. MOTOR DE INGESTA Y DISTRIBUCIÓN DE MINUTAS:
- Desarrollar la lógica de parsing para que el texto/audio de la minuta diaria no sea estático, sino que extraiga entidades clave (Action Items, Acuerdos, Responsables, Fechas Límite).
- Implementar la función asíncrona de distribución que inyecte automáticamente los compromisos extraídos hacia el módulo de tareas/micro-tareas y registre el histórico inmutable de la minuta vinculado al proyecto correspondiente.

3. DATA ROOM Y CENTRALIZACIÓN DE DOCUMENTOS (SUPABASE STORAGE):
- Implementar un servicio de subida de archivos conectado a Supabase Storage (Bucket: `documentos`), operando bajo el plan gratuito de 1GB.
- Agregar validaciones estrictas en cliente y servidor: control de tamaño máximo (5MB - 15MB) y sanitización estricta de nombres de archivos (eliminación de tildes, caracteres especiales y espacios por guiones bajos) para evitar colisiones en rutas de almacenamiento (`projects/{projectId}/{timestamp}_{filename}`).
- Registrar los metadatos del archivo subido (nombre original, ruta, tamaño, extensión y categoría) en la tabla relacional de PostgreSQL asociada al proyecto.

RESTRICCIONES TÉCNicas Y DE TRINCHERA:
- Cero dependencias de pago o servicios externos con costos ocultos. Todo debe resolverse con infraestructura gratuita (Supabase Free Tier + stack actual).
- Código limpio, tipado estricto en TypeScript, manejo defensivo de errores (`try/catch` con logs de consola limpios) y prevención estricta de condiciones de carrera.
- No romper la operación existente ni el flujo de datos actual de la herramienta,debes mejorarla
